provenance._note: R9700/gfx1201 static hardware constants (cu_count/vgprs_per_simd/max_waves_per_simd/lds_bytes_per_cu/wavefront_size) per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-01-gfx1201-phaseA-perf-instrument.md Global Constraints. lds_bytes_per_cu=65536 (64 KiB) matches the single source of truth (profiler.rs::arch_spec, used identically for every RDNA1-4 arch incl. gfx1100/gfx1200/gfx1201) and is what ROCm/HIP reports as the per-CU LDS partition; the plan prose's '128KiB' figure is the physical LDS size per WGP (shared by 2 CUs), not per-CU, and committing 131072 here would make verify_live fail loud against every real gfx1201 card. vram_mb=32768 is the R9700 (Radeon AI PRO, 32GB, hiptrx). cu_count=64 confirmed via rocminfo on the live R9700 AND the local RX 9070 XT — both are the full Navi 48 (64 CU); profiler.rs's comment lists 'RX 9070 (56 CU) / RX 9070 XT / Radeon AI PRO R9700 (64 CU)', so 64 is the R9700 value (an earlier draft used 56, the RX 9070 non-XT figure — corrected). Chip profiles are PER-DEVICE: this row describes the R9700 specifically; a different gfx1201 SKU (e.g. the 16GB RX 9070 XT) gets its own row and verify_live correctly fails on VRAM/peak_bw mismatch. peak_bw_gbps=800.0 is the theoretical GDDR6 spec constant already established by bench_gemv_hfp4g32_bw.rs::PEAK_GBPS (NOT an achieved-throughput measurement). mem_latency_ns is intentionally null/WITHHELD: Task 3 (pointer_chase_latency, GPU-required on hiptrx) has not run yet in this repo state, and the mandatory rule is that mem_latency is MEASURED, never an unlabeled estimate. Fill in via `dump_chip_profile`/`pointer_chase_latency` once Task 3 lands, then re-run verify_live on hiptrx.
